head_commit.message:
fix(tests): partial-result-preservation retry count is ceiling-bound (#9404)

* fix(tests): partial-result-preservation retry count is ceiling-bound (flaky)

The 'partial messages attached to exception chain' test asserts exactly 5
retry attempts, but the test passes an explicit 10s cumulative ceiling. The
ceiling is enforced on retry attempts (attempt > 0) in with-auto-retry; under
a slow/loaded CI runner the 5 synchronous retries (each carrying a 500ms
stream-timeout) can exceed the 10s ceiling, terminating the loop with fewer
attempts and failing the strict count assertion. This is the cause of the
release-gate failure (test job: 1106/1107) and the main CI 'test' job.

The test's own comment says it 'asserts the metadata survives, not a specific
count', so relax the assertion to >= 1 attempt (metadata survived partial
wrapping) instead of the exact 5.

* docs(metrics): sync README test-line count

head_commit.message:
fix(gsd): delivery verifier recognizes merged-to-main wave delivery (#9402)

* fix(gsd): delivery verifier recognizes merged-to-main wave delivery

When a wave's work is committed + merged to main (as the wave agent does when
executing waves step by step), the local HEAD equals origin/main and the
base-relative three-dot diff is empty — the verifier reported 'no wave target
files changed' even though the target files were changed during the campaign.
This is the same false-negative family as #9382/#9386/#9390/#9399.

Fix: thread the campaign's created-at epoch through make-delivery-verifier ->
run-delivery-verification -> check-wave-files-changed -> changed-files-set.
When created-at is known, also collect files changed in commits reachable
from HEAD since the campaign base commit (git rev-list -1 --before=<epoch>
HEAD), recognizing merged-to-main delivery as valid evidence.

Adds a regression test: without created-at the merged wave is rejected; with
created-at it is approved.

* fix(gsd): reword test comments (version-expectations) + sync README metrics

---------

head_commit.message:
fix(changelog): normalize v1.00.06 header + required sections (#9401)

The wave's CHANGELOG entry used the bracketed '## [1.00.06] - 2026-08-20'
header, but sync-readme-status's changelog-header-rx only matches the plain
'## vX.Y.Z' form. parse-changelog-top-entry therefore fell through to the
stale '## 1.00.05' header, making --check report 'README Status says
v1.00.05, q-version is v1.00.06' and breaking test-sync-readme-status.rkt
in the lint job (test shard 2/6).

Normalize the header to '## 1.00.06' and add the mandatory Breaking /
Migration / Operational sections so lint-release-notes passes.

Co-authored-by: coinerd <coinerd@users.noreply.github.com>
